metadata.title: Australia’s results from Progress in International Reading Literacy Study (PIRLS 2021)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PIRLS 2021 as a sample survey with a 2-stage stratified cluster design: schools are sampled first, and then one intact Year 4 classroom is sampled within each selected school. The report states that weights are used so that the sampled students represent the total Year 4 student population in Australia, including adjustments for intended design features (e.g., oversampling) and for non-participation. Because the analysis is based on PIRLS achievement scales derived from IRT scaling and reported means/percentages with standard errors, the weighting is consistent with complex survey estimation practices for clustered samples. The manuscript does not provide a specific weight variable name (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT), so the exact variable cannot be extracted from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: PIRLS achievement is reported on an IRT-based reading scale (mean 500, SD 100) and the report does not describe any plausible-values (PV) generation/combining or missing-data imputation/deletion strategy for the achievement estimates. Missing-data handling is therefore not documented at the level required to classify it (e.g., listwise deletion vs multiple imputation). This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, even though PIRLS scaling and survey estimation are described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The Australian PIRLS 2021 target population is Year 4 students. The report describes a national sample of 281 participating schools with at least one intact Year 4 class per school; in composite/staged classes, multiple classes could be sampled but only Year 4 students participated. Students were excluded at the national target-population stage for reasons such as very small schools, non-mainstream schools (e.g., special needs), very remote schools, and within-school exclusions including students with intellectual/functional disabilities and non-native language speakers with less than one year of exposure to English. Within sampled classes, students could also be withdrawn (left the school between sampling and assessment) and absent at the time of assessment; the assessed student count is 5,488 with 451 absent and 177 withdrawn from class/school, after 6,336 students in participating schools and 24 withdrawn from class/school and 177 excluded/withdrawn as reported in the student sample table.

data.outcome_summary: This report documents PIRLS 2021 reading literacy results for Australia (Year 4) and presents comparisons with international benchmarks and trends across cycles. PIRLS uses a matrix-sampling design with 18 booklets, each student completing one booklet containing two short texts (literary and/or informational) and associated multiple-choice and constructed-response items; achievement is scaled using item response theory to a reading scale with mean 500 and SD 100. The report uses PIRLS international benchmarks (Low 400, Intermediate 475, High 550, Advanced 625) to describe proficiency and reports the percentage of students meeting each benchmark. Sampling in Australia follows a 2-stage stratified cluster design (schools, then intact classrooms), and the report states that weights are used so sampled students represent the Year 4 population, including adjustments for design features and non-participation. Results are presented descriptively by demographic groups (e.g., gender, First Nations background), home and school context variables, and teacher/classroom factors, with standard errors and statistical significance notes; no predictive ML modeling is conducted.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an assessment results and contextual questionnaire reporting document rather than an empirical machine-learning study. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no predictive target variables, and no model performance metrics to extract; the report focuses on descriptive comparisons (means, benchmark proportions, and subgroup differences) using PIRLS scaling and survey estimation. The absence of PV-handling and missing-data-handling details reflects that the document is not a methodological ML paper and does not provide the underlying PV/missing-data pipeline used by the PIRLS scaling process.
